theme: Locks: critical sections, NSLock and os_unfair_lock

terms.definition: A part of the code that only one thread may run at a time.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let lock = NSLock()
var total = 0
lock.lock()
total += 10  // critical section
lock.unlock(); print(total)

terms.definition: A lock object that lets one thread at a time enter protected code and makes the others wait.
terms.example: Protect the counter with an NSLock.

terms.definition: A fast, low-level lock from the `os` module that must stay at one memory address.
terms.code:
import os
var lock = os_unfair_lock()
os_unfair_lock_lock(&lock)
print("locked")
os_unfair_lock_unlock(&lock)

Learn to explain how a lock protects shared data: Critical Section, NSLock & os_unfair_lock, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Critical Section - A part of the code that only one thread may run at a time.
NSLock - A lock object that lets one thread at a time enter protected code and makes the others wait.
os_unfair_lock - A fast, low-level lock from the `os` module that must stay at one memory address.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Critical Section, NSLock and os_unfair_lock in English?

dialogue.title: The slow lock
dialogue.setting: A lock that a teammate calls too slow

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I added a lock around `items`, but my teammate says it is too slow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What code is inside the lock?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Only `items.append`. That is my critical section.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. A critical section is a part of the code that only one thread may run at a time. Keep it short.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I use NSLock because it is simple.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: NSLock is fine for most apps. It lets one thread in and makes the others wait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My teammate wants os_unfair_lock instead. Is it better?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is faster, but it is low level. You must not copy an os_unfair_lock value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The lock must stay at one memory address. Copying it breaks the critical section.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I keep NSLock. Easy to read is better.
